data.title: A strange commit
story: Reading the commit history, Dimas found one message full of digits and the letters a to f. That's hexadecimal (hex): every two characters stand for one letter.
Use the Python console to turn the hex back into text, then type the flag.

artifacts.label: Commit history (git log)
artifacts.content:
a3f91c2  Fix shipping KeyError for new cities
7be0d45  Roll back release 2.3 because of checkout errors
19c4e88  practice: 464c41477b524f4c4c4241434b5f46495253547d
c02a7f1  Add Passed label to report cards

explanation: Hex is just another way to write bytes: "46" is F, "4c" is L, and so on, so bytes.fromhex() opens it without any key. That's why hex is never used to hide secrets, and a commit message should describe the change in plain words.
hints: Look for the commit message that doesn't read like a sentence.
